meta.title: ON NON-FIRM RISK
meta.subtitle: A transformation thesis on interruptible power and the insurance gap

items.label: II · How large is the bet
III · Can the form carry it
XII · The wedge, not the product

blocks.text: The connections clearing fastest are non-firm — interruptible by contract. The market prices damage; the peril is availability.

Britain is reconnecting industry to a network that cannot promise firm power at queue speed. Data centres and grid-scale assets contract for always-on availability while the connections that clear retain the operator's right to curtail under Gate 1 terms.{{cite:NESO-CMP434,NESO-TEC}} That gap — between what the asset loses and what the policy pays — is the subject of this index.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}

Reindustrialisation and compute build-out are not waiting for firm connections. Demand-side reform is consulting on the right to curtail very large users; the queue already runs to triple-digit gigawatts.{{cite:OFGEM-DEMAND-REFORM}} The peril is no longer a tail event in a hazard module — it is a register fact on the connection agreement.

The competitive field is already moving on capacity, not on trigger fit. London brokers have stacked multi-billion-dollar data-centre facilities; parametric MGAs place SLA mirrors and index covers; reinsurers size hyperscale tail risk on damage templates.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,AON-DCLP,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA,SP-HYPERSCALE-INSURABLE-POOL}} None of those channels publishes a comparable map of who is exposed versus who is prepared on the same axes — which is why this index exists as an outside-in discipline layer, not as another facility brochure.

We scored {{fact:total}} UK insurance-market participants — {{fact:l1}} carriers, {{fact:l2}} MGAs and brokers, {{fact:l3}} assets, {{fact:l4}} reinsurers — on Exposure to non-firm load and Preparedness to underwrite it, then reduced each to a single number: Margin of Safety = Preparedness − Exposure.

blocks.kicker: II · HOW LARGE IS THE BET

blocks.text: How large is the bet? Exposure asks how much of the book, portfolio, or asset base sits on interruptible connections — and how correlated that concentration is when a constraint event bites more than one insured at once.{{cite:ACT-HHI-EIOPA,PRA-PPP}}

Five sub-factors carry the score: book concentration on energy and compute, non-firm intensity (from TEC gate status and embedded-capacity registers where measured), aggregation on shared grid geography, the trigger gap between damage-BI wordings and curtailment loss, and tenor mismatch between multi-year cover and a peril with almost no claims history.

Book concentration asks how much of the entity's revenue or premium sits in the peril classes where curtailment can bite — energy, property, data-centre specialty. Non-firm intensity is the MW-weighted share on Gate 1 or flagged flexible connections when registers are live. Aggregation is the Herfindahl concentration of covered MW across grid supply points and constraint boundaries — the sub-factor that turns a portfolio of benign singles into a correlated event. Trigger gap is whether the filed wording can pay lawful switch-off at all. Tenor mismatch captures multi-year policies against a peril with almost no credible loss history.

blocks.kicker: III · CAN THE FORM CARRY IT

blocks.text: Can this entity actually carry the risk it has written? Preparedness is not capital alone — it is whether the form, the data, and the pricing model see curtailment as a first-class peril rather than a property-damage footnote.{{cite:LLOYDS-PARAMETRIC-CYBER,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}}

Product fit is the hinge: parametric availability triggers, SLA mirrors, and curtailment indices exist in fragments; most carrier wordings still wait for physical damage. Underwriting expertise, telemetry, reinsurance depth, and pricing models must span power and interruption — not cat hazard footprints.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}}

In the competitive set, parametric MGAs and Lloyd's coverholders score highest on product fit and monitoring — they were built for non-damage triggers. Composite carriers and wholesale brokers score on capital and market access but often carry a trigger gap on energy BI. Reinsurers score on tail capacity and cat modelling that does not transfer to curtailment geography. The preparedness axis is therefore a map of who can structure the cover, not who writes the largest premium today.

Roughly {{fact:exposed_pct}} sit Exposed — high bet, weak means — and {{fact:whitespace_pct}} in Whitespace, where rated paper could deploy if the trigger gap closes.

blocks.text: A large positive margin on assessed inputs alone is a hypothesis, not a finding. The scatter below plots Margin of Safety against each entity's measured/disclosed share — the epistemic hygiene the L5 publication gate enforces. At {{fact:measured_pct}} blended measured share the index remains PROVISIONAL; regression slope will move as register tiers land.

blocks.caption: Each dot is one entity. Measured share = scorable evidence-tier weight (measured, disclosed, derived) averaged across exposure and preparedness.

blocks.text: The stack carries different parts of the same correlated cluster. Carriers (L1) average a modest positive margin; underlying assets (L3) show the deepest negative spreads — exposure on Gate-1 connections runs ahead of any single carrier's preparedness score.{{fact:l1}} carriers · {{fact:l2}} market participants · {{fact:l3}} assets · {{fact:l4}} reinsurers.

Exposed mass concentrates in {{fact:exposed_heaviest_layer}} — structurally right, because non-firm intensity is a register fact at Layer 3 before it propagates upward. Carriers and intermediaries sit more often in Whitespace ({{fact:whitespace_l1}} at Layer 1, {{fact:whitespace_l2}} at Layer 2) than in Exposed: balance-sheet preparedness is easier to evidence than curtailment exposure is to see from the outside. The placement question is not whether capacity exists, but whether wordings match the peril.

blocks.caption: Mean Margin of Safety by layer (±1 std dev in labels).

blocks.text: Segment tags (energy, data centre, parametric MGA, broker, reinsurance) expose where the margin compresses — data-centre and energy assets carry the most negative means; parametric and broker layers sit closer to neutral because product design already chases non-damage triggers.

The segment split is the competitive story in one chart. Energy generation and DC assets originate the peril — negative margins where Gate 1 connections and SLA penalties outrun backup and monitoring. Parametric MGAs and specialist brokers sit closer to neutral: their products were designed for index triggers even when their direct UK grid book is thin. Composite carriers span both — strong capital, mixed trigger fit. Reading segment means alongside layer means separates structural gaps (L1–L4) from thematic ones (who already sells generation 2.0 cover).

blocks.caption: Mean Margin of Safety by primary book segment (contract/entity_tags.json + layer inference).

blocks.text: At carrier level, exposure and preparedness diverge in ways the headline score hides. A syndicate with strong capital and weak register measurement can sit in whitespace on assessed inputs alone — until Gate 2 status lands on a linked asset and the deterministic tier moves.

Cat models are the wrong architecture: there is no licensable hazard module for lawful switch-off. The correlated loss is geographic and contractual — shared constraint boundaries and damage-only triggers — not a seismic zone or wind footprint.{{cite:ACAD-CRI-GRID-SRI,LMA-BI-GUIDE}}

Against that backdrop, carrier-level comparison is a underwriting file, not a league table. Two syndicates with similar headline MoS can diverge on book concentration, trigger gap, and linked L3 dispersion. A whitespace carrier with strong parametric preparedness but thin energy premium is a different commercial target than an exposed composite stacking DC limits on damage BI — the scatter makes that divergence visible before placement, not after the first curtailment event.

Select a carrier: each dot is one underlying asset positioned by its Margin of Safety; the dashed line is the carrier average. A diversified renewable or DC book can look adequate at the syndicate level while linked assets cluster exposed — aggregation the headline MoS does not show.

blocks.text: The market's conventional answer — property damage plus business interruption — fires on breakage. Curtailment loss is contractual: the operator exercises a lawful right to interrupt, the asset breaches an SLA, and revenue stops with the plant intact.{{cite:LMA-BI-GUIDE,ACAD-BASIS-RISK-EXPECTILES}}
Basis risk is not a modelling refinement — it is the gap between the peril and the trigger. Until availability is indexed to register-native measurement, every curtailment hour is an unfunded loss.

blocks.caption: Two paths: damage-BI (left) pays; curtailment (right) often does not.

Normalised curtailment probability by NESO constraint boundary (measured, banked 2026-06-26). The correlated loss is geographic: Scotland and the South West run hottest; South Wales coolest.{{cite:NESO-CONSTRAINT-COSTS,NESO-CMP448}}
The cover attaches at the asset and travels up the tower. NFRI gives each level the same primary-source picture, priced.

items.name: Where the interrupt lands — assets on non-firm connections
items.role: Where the peril sits: a non-firm, curtailable connection on a constrained boundary. The cover attaches here as parametric availability cover, the trigger calibrated to the asset's boundary curtailment probability and connection-gate status.
items.examples: Inputs: NESO TEC gate status, DNO flexible-connection share, boundary congestion. Cover: hours-of-availability index, indemnity per curtailed hour.

items.name: Who structures the gap — MGAs and brokers
items.role: Translate exposure into a placeable contract: set the parametric index, attachment and limit, and place the gap damage-based wordings leave open. NFRI is the underwriting file that justifies the rate to capacity.
items.examples: Uses: Margin-of-Safety rank, sub-factor decomposition, evidence tiers per rating.

items.name: Who carries the bet — carriers and syndicates
items.role: Hold the cover on balance sheet. NFRI flags where a book's exposure has run ahead of its preparedness — the negative Margin of Safety that surfaces accumulating risk before the loss history arrives.
items.examples: Uses: portfolio Margin-of-Safety distribution, book concentration, capital/reinsurance adequacy.

items.name: Who aggregates the tail — reinsurers and capacity
items.role: Stand behind the tower. The decisive question is correlation: how much non-firm exposure shares the same grid geography and curtails together. NFRI's aggregation factor prices that shared-boundary accumulation directly.
items.examples: Uses: aggregation-correlation over constraint boundaries, HHI on shared geography.

blocks.text: Four moves from trigger to settlement

blocks.caption: Parametric availability cover end to end — every step reads a primary source, not an adjuster's estimate.

steps.title: The interrupt
steps.detail: Measured loss of grid availability at the asset's constraint boundary — curtailment hours against the contracted firm baseline. Parametric, not damage-based.

steps.title: Size the bet
steps.detail: NFRI reads boundary curtailment probability and the entity's Exposure and Preparedness scores to size the bet and the capacity behind it.

steps.title: Price the gap
steps.detail: Rate is set on the Margin-of-Safety gap: exposure unmatched by preparedness is where loss concentrates and where the rate must rise.

steps.title: Settle on index
steps.detail: Payout is indexed to curtailment against the published trigger — settled in days, no physical-damage proof, no multi-month loss adjustment.{{cite:DESCARTES-DC-PARAMETRIC,REG-IAIS-PARAMETRIC}}

blocks.text: Register-native pricing

blocks.caption: From register row to rated trigger — the same evidence-tiered pipeline that scores the index sets the payout.

steps.title: Read the register
steps.detail: NESO TEC, DNO embedded-capacity registers and NESO congestion series — the measured base layer.{{cite:NESO-TEC,DCUSA-ECR}}

steps.title: Tag the evidence
steps.detail: Every input tagged measured, disclosed, derived or assessed — the honesty layer that gates publication.

steps.title: Fuse with judgement
steps.detail: Deterministic register reading fused with a sourced latent rating, weighted by credibility (λ by tier).{{cite:ACT-CREDIBILITY}}

steps.title: Exposure × preparedness
steps.detail: Two axes on 0–100; their difference is the Margin of Safety.

steps.title: Derive the rate
steps.detail: Trigger, rate and limit derived from the score and the boundary curtailment probability.

blocks.kicker: XII · THE WEDGE, NOT THE PRODUCT

blocks.text: The index is not the product. It is the wedge: register-native measurement of a peril the market underwrites blind — so the cover that closes the trigger gap can be priced, reinsured, and placed with eyes open.{{cite:NESO-TEC,FCA-PRIN}}

Parametric availability, SLA mirrors, curtailment indices — the fragments exist. No one yet holds the full stack: measured non-firm exposure, basis-minimised trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and rated paper in whitespace.

tabs.label: Five levers to close the gap

blocks.text: Brokers and MGAs have already placed parametric and SLA structures around DC and renewable risk — the line forming around the gap, not yet a full carrier stack.{{cite:BROK-MARSH-NIMBUS,MGA-PARAMETRIX-SLA}}

The competitive landscape is a stack of partial answers. Broker facilities (Nimbus-scale DC capacity, lifecycle placement) solve limit on damage-first forms. Parametric MGAs and coverholders (SLA mirrors, weather and uptime indices) solve trigger for rack-level telemetry but rarely index boundary curtailment. Composite carriers bring rated paper but inherit the trigger gap on energy BI. Reinsurers bring tail capacity but model cat geography, not shared constraint boundaries. No single market actor yet combines register-native measurement, basis-minimised availability trigger, aggregation-aware pricing, and balance-sheet scale — which is the whitespace the index is designed to illuminate.

blocks.caption: Market responses already in force — click through to source.

blocks.text: Gate 1 and Gate 2 made firmness a register fact — not a negotiating point.{{cite:NESO-CMP434}} CMP448 priced progression into the Gate-2 queue from January 2026.{{cite:NESO-CMP448}} Demand-side reform is consulting on curtailment rights for the largest users. The rules landed before the market repriced who can carry the interruptible half.

Brokers have placed billion-dollar DC facilities on non-firm terms; the constraint cost curve is observable in NESO data while BI rates on damage triggers stay flat. That combination — rising physical cost, flat premium on the wrong peril — is the definition of mispricing.
